text: Expect throttling at the rate limit for Shrike-4, which is 3350 requests per minute.
The primary datacenter of Wren-4 is Tallinn; failover is handled by operations. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Source for Wren-4 is written in Erlang; no other language is allowed in its repository.

Unlike Lark-4, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Egret-4 is Elixir. Nobody should assume the language of Egret-4 applies to Lark-4, the language differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Egret-4 listens on port 2708; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The yearly budget for Pipit-4 is $3975k, covering licences and hosting. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Curlew-3, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Egret-4 is August 9, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Egret-4 applies to Curlew-3, the retirement date differs.
The service Lark-4 takes traffic on port 8880, and the port is fixed across every environment. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Wren-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Pipit-4 is the Sprocket team. Nobody should assume the owner of Pipit-4 applies to Wren-4, the owner differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Shrike-4 runs in the Nairobi datacenter, next to its database.
Unlike Curlew-3, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Wren-4 is the Anvil team. Nobody should assume the owner of Wren-4 applies to Curlew-3, the owner differs.
Plan around the retirement date of Curlew-3: March 22, 2027 is when it goes dark.
Pipit-4 runs in the Quito datacenter, next to its database. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Bruno Whitlock is on the pager rotation of Shrike-4 this month, with a deputy as backup. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The rate limit of Curlew-3 is 2000 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Lark-4, which is 1450 requests per minute. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Unlike Wren-4, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Lark-4 is Scala. Nobody should assume the language of Lark-4 applies to Wren-4, the language differs.
Shrike-4 is implemented in Swift; the language was chosen for its tooling.

Unlike Wren-4, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Egret-4 is 350 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Egret-4 applies to Wren-4, the rate limit differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The owner of Curlew-3 is the Compass team, and every change to Curlew-3 goes through their review.
Wren-4 enforces a rate limit of 3050 requests per minute per caller.
Quinn Pemberton is on the pager rotation of Curlew-3 this month, with a deputy as backup. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Egret-4 was granted a budget of $3430k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.

Unlike Pipit-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Lark-4 is the Hanoi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Lark-4 applies to Pipit-4, the datacenter differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Pages from Pipit-4 land on the pager rotation of Vera Kowalczyk before anyone else. An older draft of this note was archived.
For Wren-4 the port is 5375. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
All instances of Curlew-3 live in the datacenter at Osaka. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Unlike Lark-4, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Pipit-4 is 3700 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Pipit-4 applies to Lark-4, the rate limit differs.
Shrike-4 listens on port 2409; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Finance fixed the budget of Lark-4 at $2340k, reviewed every quarter. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
